summary: 6,407 generators tracked monthly across published vintages. 69 percent saw a first revision and 44 percent saw one of two months or more; the median first revision arrives five months after a project first appears; between annual snapshots the modal revision is exactly twelve months, so movement accumulates in whole-year steps.
note: Truths T1 to T4. No counterpart in the expanded manifest yet.

summary: Of 721 generators promised in 2015 and running by 2023, 64 percent arrived late: median two months late, worst eighty-three. A real delivery is a label, never an input.
note: Truth T4.

summary: 711 promised generators were formally cancelled or postponed. Together with revisions of six months or more, cancellation is the tail where the information lives, because 36 percent of first revisions are a nudge of one month or less.
note: Truths T1 and T2.

summary: The binding constraint on energising capacity (truth T11) and the highest value missing dataset. No queue source reached from this host: ERCOT timed out, PJM and CAISO untested, and the national lab and DOE files are not usable.
note: Blocked by access, not by modelling.

summary: 1,285 filers report remaining performance obligations at least three times between 2015Q1 and 2024Q3. 382 fall in a declared industry group and 903 form a placebo, giving 4,634 usable timestamped revisions. Nothing is both meaningful and strong in the predicted direction, and the date placebo produced seven cells above two sigma against two in the real data.
note: Truth T7 and the breadth test.

summary: The closest structured trace of a slip, with a median lag of 94 days from period end to public availability for PWR. The tag stops being used after 2017, so the series has no recent history and cannot carry a current study.
note: Truth T5; registry marks it thin.

summary: XBRL facts joined to filing acceptance times, so the commitment series is point in time. Used as a feature in the delivery models; no standalone measurement summary of this node is written yet.
note: The representation exists; the planet sheet is incomplete.

summary: Hourly balancing-authority demand from EIA-930 with a declared publication lag. The panel is readable; no measurement summary of this node alone is written yet.
note: Registry declares the representation; the modelling write-up is the gap.

summary: Hourly generation by fuel from EIA-930 with a declared publication lag. The panel is readable; no measurement summary of this node alone is written yet.
note: Registry declares the representation; the modelling write-up is the gap.

summary: Weekly US Drought Monitor severity with release dates. Three factor sets including drought failed to move the chance that a promise is revised, and the drought coefficient points the wrong way, so this node is recorded as having no payer rather than a weak effect.
note: Truth T10 and the drought decision in the ledger.

summary: Ten GPU families and 5,423 family days across two regions, June 2022 to March 2024. The median pairwise correlation of daily price changes is minus 0.01, so compute is ten separate markets rather than one. The series is provider-listed spot pricing per instance hour, a policy rather than a clearing price, and it clears its own null against none of eleven partners.
note: Truths T8 and T9; the one clear crosswalk found.

summary: What compute actually rents for in executed transactions rather than listed prices. Only current values are public; the full history is a paid tier.
note: Would close the policy-versus-clearing-price gap in T9.

summary: The price at which scarcity is actually paid. No settlement point source reached from this host; ERCOT did not respond and PJM and CAISO remain untested.
note: Blocked by access.

summary: Used as a control everywhere. The one mechanism-relevant scan survivor, firm disclosure revisions against gas, is plus 0.31 in the data-centre group but minus 0.06 in the contractor and equipment groups, so it belongs to the comparison group rather than to the mechanism.
note: Specificity test in the scan section of the note.

summary: A known macro link with rates and one of the two survivors that remain inside the mechanism window. It is asset co-movement, not a relation that belongs to this mechanism, and it is reported as a control.
note: Note section 5.

summary: A listed proxy with a daily close, used as a control. It survives the scan inside its own family, which is co-movement rather than a mechanism edge.
note: Note section 5.

summary: The discount rate long-lived projects are valued against, used as a control in every study. Its scan relations are the known utilities and copper links.
note: Note section 5.

summary: Equal-weight basket of the firms that build and equip the infrastructure, 81 overlapping months with the scarcity basket, change correlation plus 0.53 and level correlation plus 0.89 at the 100th percentile of its null. The two baskets are one risk viewed twice, which is why the pair's shared factor is its main tail risk.
note: Note sections 5 and 6.

summary: Equal-weight basket of the firms whose revenue comes from power and capacity being scarce; the other leg of the one-risk pair above.
note: Note sections 5 and 6.

summary: A contract between two named companies, filed and timestamped, but enumerated for four firms only, and the counterparty must be extracted from exhibit text. Coverage is the binding limit, not the timestamp.
note: Registry marks it thin.

summary: What leveraged participants pay to hold a position, a crowding read. Crypto history is long but unrelated to this mechanism, and the two non-crypto markets only reach back to 2025-08-29.
note: Truth T13 and the cascade protocol.

summary: What the option market expects an event to do to a price, the benchmark the bonus challenge is scored against. No entitlement is held for historical option chains.
note: The single most valuable entitlement for the options expression.

summary: Survey and backlog reading from FRED with declared lags, used in the delivery factor models. No standalone measurement summary of this node is written yet.
note: The modelling write-up is the gap.

summary: 339 event legs recorded from 2015-07 to 2022-09, and zero eligible return rows, because primary clocks and pre-effective quantities are missing. The provider's own announcement archive and fund holdings history are not yet acquired; a third-party list is not an authoritative substitute.
note: The instrument-side gap is data, not method.

summary: The quantity dealers must transact to keep delta and gamma inside limits. Historical option chains are not entitled, so the surface cannot be reconstructed and the flow cannot be inferred.
note: Blocked by entitlement.

summary: Segment revenue gives a read on the object but not a rate: one large landlord is about 99 percent rental revenue and one small host about half, while leases are reported in aggregate, so a per-unit rate needs lease-level disclosures that are not systematically available.
note: Truth T15 and the credit layer.

summary: The capital a project draws as milestones are certified. Drawdown timing is only visible through periodic filings, never as a flow, and the per-deal instrument at the site level is blocked by a data entitlement.
note: The per-site credit door.

summary: The chain itself. Four broad searches are null: the firm price test (84 revisions, every |t| below 1.3 in the predicted direction), the breadth test (4,634 events, placebo over-produced), the aggregate strategy (development net minus 0.15 percent a month at doubled costs; the opened window's next-year cell plus 0.27 but one-signed in 89 percent of months), and the scan (no cross-family survivor against 0.9 and 1.1 expected). The mechanism is real and the expression is unsolved.
note: Truth T12; the standing problem is linkage and instrument.

summary: 382 firms and 4,634 timestamped revisions at horizons of one to twenty sessions: no association with the disclosing firm's own price, and shuffled dates produced more nominally significant cells than real ones.
note: Truth T7.

summary: The aggregate strategy, net of costs. Development: next-year plus 0.07 percent a month at 10 basis points, minus 0.15 at doubled costs; the balanced definition minus 0.30 and minus 0.53. The opened window adds a positive next-year cell (plus 0.45 / plus 0.27) that is the buildout-versus-scarcity regime spread in a near-static pair, not signal. Drawdowns reach minus 48 percent.
note: The tradability gate failed; the record is results/ and docs/plan/sealed-test-record.md.

summary: The claim that the market underreacts to a disclosed revision. Not supported in the covered expression, which is efficient (truth T7), so any remaining chance is in an uncovered subset of names or in a different instrument.
note: The claim is labelled descriptive at most.

summary: The aggregate credit expression: 48 declared tests, seven nominal hits against 2.40 expected, zero survivors after rate control across the grid. On the long window, 24 tests gave nine nominal hits against 1.20 expected and six Benjamini-Hochberg survivors, but half the effect lives in ten days, the two carrying measures load with opposite signs on the same names, effective breadth is 0.62 bets, and none of the six clear a two-legged 20 basis point round trip.
note: The per-site door needs an entitlement.

summary: The EDGAR deal registry the credit layer was built on: issuer, series, pool structure, ratings and diligence rows, each tied to a filing. It is the source layer for the credit tests, and the aggregate expression built on it is null.
note: Downstream of EDGAR only.

summary: The gate that every number in the note comes from a committed file under results/, produced by code in this repo, with make check and make test green and the public credential scan clean.
note: The cap rule's first condition.

summary: The declared event-study design: matched sector benchmark, signal usable at acceptance plus a processing lag, fills at the first session strictly after. Fifty cells, nothing meaningful in the predicted direction.
note: Design and result are separate owners.

summary: The issuer identity layer. It is the bottleneck for attribution: only 6.2 percent of slipped capacity sits with an entity carrying a large listed owner, because 80 percent sits in project and holding companies.
note: Truth T6; the crosswalk is the live work.
